Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

derive verb

get (pleasure, profit, comfort) from something

also derive pleasure from, derive benefit from, get out of, draw from

classical

Plaut. Am. 2.2.9: plūs aegrī ex abitū virī quam ex adventū voluptātis cēpī (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 361: magnam voluptātem capere ex

capiō, capere, cēpī, captum

verb, third conjugation (-iō), with ex and the ablative · Conjugation on Wiktionary

get, take (pleasure, profit, grief) from

With nouns of feeling and gain: voluptātem, dolōrem, frūctum capere ex. The verb’s first sense is “take, seize” (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • percipiō, percipere, percēpī, perceptum — receive, gather; feel (pleasure, grief)

    verb, third conjugation (-iō), with ex and the ablative · also used · classical · Cic. Fin. 1.63: voluptātem … percipī (Lewis & Short) · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Literally to gather in (a harvest: percipere frūctūs, Cic. Sen. 24); also to perceive, learn. Somewhat weightier than capere.

  • 1tractum: short a. Lachmann’s law does not lengthen before an old aspirate or a voiceless stop: the house ruling of 9 November 2026 (with Allen’s trăctus, against Bennett’s trāctus). Ruling: Lachmann’s law: āctus, lēctus, frāctus.

    trahō1, trahere, trāxī, tractum — draw, get (something, often unwelcome) from

    verb, third conjugation, with ex and the ablative · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 4.3.1: molestiam trāxerit (Lewis & Short: “has derived, i.e. has received, suffered”) · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    First “drag, pull”.

Examples

  • plūs aegrī ex abitū virī quam ex adventū voluptātis cēpī

    I got more grief from my husband’s going than pleasure from his comingPlaut. Am. 2.2.9 (Lewis & Short)

  • neque majōrem voluptātem ex īnfīnītō tempore aetātis percipī posse, quam ex hōc percipiātur

    that no greater pleasure can be had from an endless lifetime than is had from this (finite) oneCic. Fin. 1.63 (Lewis & Short)

  • Magnam ex hortō voluptātem capimus.

    We get a lot of pleasure out of the garden.composed

See also benefit, enjoy, derive.

SourcesLewis & Short: capio · Lewis & Short: percipio · Lewis & Short: traho

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.

The example sentences marked “composed” are ours.
